operational_records.name: Population normalization with spatially local inhibition
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: antennal-lobe inhibition produces divisive normalization; APL inhibition within the mushroom body can be spatially localized. These are convergent examples of normalization, not two independent general learning algorithms. The localized APL result specifically argues against equating the entire biological circuit with one global scalar.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes pooling neighborhoods and gains; lifetime activity varies without requiring weight learning. Proposed rate approximation: pool_p = sum of locally connected activities; output_i = drive_i / (epsilon + gain * pool_p). A neuronal pooling unit supplies the denominator, rather than a synapse reading the whole network.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Already-covered inhibition/sparsity family. The September ledger records scalar APL work; local neighborhoods are a variant, not a newly discovered family.

operational_records.name: Adaptive temporal filtering
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: fly olfactory receptor responses have adaptive temporal dynamics, and spike generation adds temporal filtering. This supports a computation over recent history; it does not show durable rule learning.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes time constants and filter signs. Proposed local state rule: a_next = (1-alpha)*a + alpha*x; output = phi(x - beta*a). This is activity-state adaptation, not a weight update. Do not relabel every adaptation time constant as a separate mechanism.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: The historical ledger already contains temporal-contrast/fast-minus-slow sensory variants. This is a source-grounded reference, not an untested recommendation.

operational_records.name: Learned inhibition of familiar background
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown/inferred: targeted experiments implicate local inhibitory plasticity in odor-specific habituation. This differs from F02: the relevant effective inhibition changes with experience rather than merely tracking a fast adaptation state. A complete synapse-by-synapse learning equation was not measured. Sudhakaran et al. (2012) provides a follow-up dissection of recurrent inhibitory pathways, but is not independent replication by a wholly separate research group.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes partners. A proposed, not experimentally identified, inhibitory update is: delta inhibitory_magnitude = eta * local_presynaptic_activity * (target_activity - target_rate). It increases inhibition when the target is too active. A familiarity/exposure gate must be locally supplied if used; semantic irrelevance cannot be assumed.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Overlaps inhibitory adaptation and existing input-side plasticity. No claim that a particular MiniFly implementation is untested.

operational_records.name: Input-side timing-dependent plasticity
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: timing-dependent changes at incoming PN→KC synapses can facilitate olfactory learning, with dopaminergic involvement. This is not merely KC→MBON valence writing at the output. It supplies a specific alternative locus for adapting representations.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes sparse partners; lifetime PN→KC magnitudes are plastic. Proposed abstraction: delta w_ij = eta * local_timing_kernel(pre_i, post_j) * local_modulator_j, followed by sign-preserving bounds. The paper supports timing sensitivity, not this exact universal factorization or a particular numerical kernel.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Explicitly present as ITDP/M10 in the September pruning ledger. Keep as a mechanistically specified variant, not a newly found idea.

operational_records.name: Timing-sensitive, signed associative writing
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: odor-linked KC→MBON plasticity can be induced by appropriately timed dopamine, and timing can change the sign of the resulting association/plasticity. These findings justify a timing-sensitive local teaching mechanism. They do not establish a universal pre×post×dopamine rule at every such synapse.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes compartments; life changes individual KC→MBON magnitudes. Proposed abstraction: eligibility_next = lambda*eligibility + local_activity_event; delta w = eta*eligibility*signed_local_teaching_signal. A timing kernel or opponent teaching channels determine sign. The effective predictor update must be translated consistently into depression/potentiation of an excitatory physical synapse.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Baseline/retained family: local writing and eligibility already exist in the historical project. Synaptic tagging, eligibility and consolidation should not be counted as synonyms or automatically as three new modules.

operational_records.name: Compartment-specific teaching channels
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: adult DAN cell types write and update memories with different dynamics. Larval connectomics and modeling show substantial recurrent organization around teaching neurons. This supports heterogeneous teaching channels; it does not establish independent, arbitrary target vectors for every neuron.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development sets the routing matrix and a small number C of channel types. Proposed lifetime update: delta w_ic = eta_c * e_ic * d_c. Each d_c must be computed by its local circuit from allowed inputs. C independent external target errors are not silently equivalent to one scalar reward.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Already-covered compartment heterogeneity/teaching allocation. More compartments are not automatically new mechanisms.

operational_records.name: Activity-dependent amplification of teaching
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: reciprocal KC–DAN connectivity includes a positive feedback contribution required for learning. This is an amplification loop, not evidence that the loop subtracts an expected reward.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes feedback weights and saturation. Proposed dynamics: d_next = clip(external_teaching + gain*sum(local_KC_activity), 0, d_max). Lifetime KC→MBON plasticity remains F05. A learned feedback matrix would be another plastic site requiring its own rule.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Overlaps the retained MB output/teaching loop. Do not conflate this operation with the error subtraction in F08 or the transfer of teacher status in F09.

operational_records.name: Prediction-error computation in an MB output–teaching loop
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Proposed and tested in models: output-neuron predictions feed back to dopamine-like teaching signals, allowing error-driven rather than absolute-reinforcement updates. Conditioning and blocking simulations are evidence for the model’s behavior, not direct proof that all fly DANs implement this calculation.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes circuit signs/routing; life changes effective predictor weights. Minimal local model: prediction = sum_i(v_i*x_i); delta = reward - prediction; e_i_next = lambda*e_i + x_i; delta v_i = eta*delta*e_i. The target/output orientation determines the corresponding physical KC→MBON update sign. No hidden-layer gradient follows from this equation.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Potentially an already implemented teacher-quality mechanism. The exact current MiniFly feedback computation has not been re-audited in this review.

operational_records.name: A learned cue becomes a teacher for another association
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: second-order conditioning uses a hierarchy in which a learned reward-predicting cue can recruit teaching for another compartment. Rachad et al. (2025) supplies convergent circuit/behavioral/model evidence for higher-order associative chains. This is stronger than merely observing anatomical recurrence, but remains distinct from learning a reusable arithmetic operation.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes teacher→intermediary→student routes. Proposed abstraction: d_student = external_reward + alpha*teacher_output; delta w_student = eta*student_eligibility*d_student. Teacher output must be learned from experience, not supplied from labels at test time. The full biological update and safeguards against self-reinforcing false predictions remain incompletely identified.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Subfamily of existing MB feedback and fast/slow compartments, but teaching transfer is an identifiable extra operation. Current exact implementation status unknown.

operational_records.name: State-dependent readout and disinhibitory routing
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: motivational state can gate memory expression, and learning/motivation can alter feed-forward inhibition in the MB output network. Failure to express a behavior is therefore not automatically loss of the stored association.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes routes. Proposed readout: output = g(state)*memory_output, with a small fixed state-to-gain map; a more explicit version uses two inhibitory stages. The evidence does not specify a generally sufficient local rule for learning arbitrary context keys. Changing state can alter reads without changing stored weights.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Existing internal-state gating family and overlaps the separate attention/WM survey. No new generic “add a gate” recommendation.

operational_records.name: Opposing learned memories rather than overwriting one trace
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: extinction can involve a parallel opposing memory that competes with the original association. This is not the claim that all forgetting is erasure or that every inhibitory response is a separate memory system.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes two opposing channels. Proposed effective output: value = original_prediction - opponent_prediction. Both channels can use bounded locally modulated associative updates; omitted expected reinforcement trains the opponent only if that omission signal is explicitly computed. This equation is an abstraction, not the measured complete biological rule.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Overlaps banks, compartmental retention and revision already screened. Include as a mechanistic distinction, not another broad memory-management proposal.

operational_records.name: Bounded post-event teaching reverberation
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown/inferred: recurrent reward-related activity contributes to appetitive long-term memory, while inhibitory feedback helps regulate dopaminergic activity. These studies concern different circuit details, so their combination into one controller is proposed. Matsuno et al. (2026) links aberrant post-training dopamine to maladaptive memory broadening, not useful rule generalization.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes loop gains and negative-feedback topology. Proposed two-state controller: d_next = clip((1-a)*d + b*event - c*z,0,d_max); z_next = (1-h)*z + h*d. d gates already eligible local writes. Eligibility must decay or reset so unrelated later inputs are not captured. This is bounded teaching persistence, not an archive replay buffer.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Already-covered consolidation/termination family. Keep separate from replay but do not launch it instead of the user-described replay controls.

operational_records.name: Re-anchor new sensory renderings to a stable internal coordinate
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: the visual input associated with an internal heading representation can be reorganized by sensorimotor experience. Convergent 2019 studies connect stable heading dynamics with adaptable visual mapping. The exact synaptic learning law is inferred/proposed, not directly measured in full. A December 2025 preprint by Plitt et al. reports that octopaminergic feedback conveys heading activity to sensory presynaptic terminals and is necessary/sufficient for the tested anchoring plasticity; this newer claim remains provisional.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes the compass kernel; life changes sensory-to-state anchoring. Proposed inhibitory-association variant: delta a_ij = -eta*visual_i*state_j + slow_local_restoration(a_ij), with nonnegative inhibitory magnitudes. Weakening coactive inhibition can anchor the cue to the occupied state. The exact rule/bounds need validation; a privileged correct-state target is not allowed. The preprint motivates replacing direct state_j in the update by a locally delivered modulatory state signal m_j. That spatially structured feedback is not a single uniform global reward scalar and must be explicitly implemented and budgeted.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Family overlap with input plasticity and the already-tested CX. Whether the exact sensory-anchor variant was tested is unknown; it must not be announced as new.

operational_records.name: Continuous recurrent working state
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown/inferred through perturbation and modeling: fly heading populations have ring-attractor dynamics. This supports persistent low-dimensional state. It does not establish a locally learned general working-memory program.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes a translation-structured recurrent kernel. Proposed dynamics: h_next = phi(K*h + B*motion - inhibition); the stable bump encodes state. No lifetime weight changes are necessary for this computation. Sensory anchoring plasticity is F13, not evidence of a plastic ring kernel.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Already-reviewed/tested central-complex family. Exact implementation details were not inspected here.

operational_records.name: Accumulate evidence before committing
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: subthreshold dendritic activity in αβ-core KCs integrates olfactory evidence on behaviorally relevant decision timescales. This is a within-neuron temporal computation, not evidence that recurrent weights were learned for the task.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes integration/threshold parameters. Proposed state rule: z_next = (1-leak)*z + evidence; commit when z reaches threshold, then reset. A signed evidence difference requires separately specified opponent inputs. No weight plasticity is required for the accumulator.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Overlap with the recurrent-state/integration family; more specific than adding a generic RNN. Current exact implementation unknown.

operational_records.name: Coordinate transformation by population-vector combination
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown/inferred from recordings and circuit organization: fan-shaped-body pathways combine movement-related signals to represent allocentric travelling direction. This is a coordinate transformation, not proof of a complete learned home-vector integrator or universal addition engine. Ishida et al. (2026) further shows a population-vector inversion operation associated with a change in firing mode. Inversion is recorded here as a distinct operator within the vector-computation family, not padded into another broad family.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes phase offsets and coupling. Mathematical abstraction: world_vector = rotation(heading) * body_vector; a population implementation sums appropriately shifted component codes. This is a runtime operation; no local learning law is needed for fixed couplings. Learning what a raw byte denotes remains outside the circuit. For the inversion variant, the mathematical operation is v_out = -v_in, represented as a half-turn of population phase; this does not imply negative firing rates.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Already-reviewed/tested CX family. No novelty claim for generic vector addition.

operational_records.name: Compare current state with a goal in a common coordinate
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: fly steering circuitry transforms heading/goal information into lateralized commands. Convergent 2024 studies identify how such comparisons can drive goal-oriented steering. Their findings do not supply a general local rule for learning all goals from sparse reward.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes comparison topology. Proposed abstraction: left = max(0, sin(goal-heading)); right = max(0, sin(heading-goal)). Goal is bounded activity state, not an unexplained task label. A learned goal-setting policy needs an additional local algorithm, which this comparison does not provide.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Part of the existing central-complex/goal family; not another independent source of generic learning capacity.

operational_records.name: Multiplicative interaction through excitation and disinhibition
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown with recordings and conductance-based simulation: coincident excitation and release from inhibition produce a multiplication-like nonlinearity in T4 motion neurons. This is an analogue approximation over an operating range, not exact arbitrary signed multiplication.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes input placement/gains. Proposed computational abstraction: output = phi(excitatory_input) * gate(local_disinhibition). Both signals must arrive physically at the neuron. No lifetime synaptic learning is required for the interaction; learning operands or routing into it is a separate problem.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Potentially a specific variant within the previously reviewed gain/routing family; not established as untested in MiniFly.

operational_records.name: Predict and cancel self-generated sensory input
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown: motor-related signals counteract expected visual consequences in fly visuomotor neurons. This supports an efference-copy/cancellation computation; it does not demonstrate a general predictive-coding learning rule.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development supplies a motor-to-sensory prediction map. Runtime: residual = sensory_input - predicted_input(action_copy). A possible lifetime adaptation delta w = eta*action_feature*local_residual is proposed, not established by the cited experiment. The residual must be present at the receiving neuron.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Related to predictive/residual mechanisms, not a synonym for cortical backpropagation. Current exact MiniFly coverage unknown.

operational_records.name: Priority competition that produces a sequence
operational_records.source_evidence_claim: Shown/inferred through perturbation: competing grooming programs are organized by suppression relationships; removal of a dominant drive allows another program to emerge. This is innate behavioral sequencing, not demonstrated learning of arbitrary routines.
operational_records.source_computational_proposal: Development fixes priority edges. Proposed dynamics: select the highest currently active unsuppressed drive; execution reduces that drive, releasing the next program. No life weight learning is claimed. To learn a different priority graph would require an additional mechanism and rule.
operational_records.source_overlap_claim: Computational reference only. The historical screen explicitly excluded downstream motor programs from the persistent-memory core; this is not being promoted into the immediate plan.
